note: Set A and Set B are nearly identical on their shared claims, but A additionally captures the North Living door frame & wall trim finish P4 ("& WALL TRIM FIN. W/ P4"), a real note on the page that B omits entirely; B's only unique claim is the P2 finish with a redundant condition. Both sets make the same misbindings (South Bedroom's 1'-5 3/4" and 2 5/8" heights and the 4 1/2"/4 1/4" top offsets attributed to North Living, dimensions tied to the grid letters "E" and "B") and both add the invented condition "artwork center point" to the 4'-3" dimension. Because A keeps both finish callouts (P2 and P4) while B drops one important fact, A is the better set.
remarks: Shared errors in both sets: (1) 1'-5 3/4" and 2 5/8" are right-side dimensions of the SOUTH BEDROOM (A1) elevation, not North Living; (2) in North Living the top segments read 4 1/4" (left) and 4 1/2" (right), so the 'left offset 4 1/2" / right offset 4 1/4"' pair is swapped (it matches the South Bedroom layout); (3) 'Interior Elevation E/B' are grid-line letters, not elevation entities, so those dimension bindings are unsupported; (4) the condition 'vertical distance from floor to artwork center point' is not stated anywhere on the page (only 'SEE ARTWORK PKG FOR SIZE & MOUNT LOCATIONS'); (5) 9'-11 1/2" and the scale are each stated twice under two attribute names. Both sets also miss the South Bedroom overall height 9' - 2" and the A1 South Bedroom scale 1/2" = 1'-0". The small 7" dimension near P3/P4 is too small to verify confidently at this image resolution. Note that the two 'Door Frame & Wall Trim finish' facts belong to different elevations (P4 = North Living, P2 = South Bedroom); neither set binds them to an elevation, so the entity name alone is ambiguous.
